source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Deep vein thrombosis, which is characteristically relieved promptly by rest after a predictable walking distance.","B":"Restless legs syndrome, which typically produces reproducible ischemic calf pain only during exertion.","C":"Intermittent claudication from lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, reflecting exertional ischemia.","D":"A normal effect of aging that does not warrant vascular assessment when symptoms resolve with rest."}}
source_row.rationale: NHLBI describes PAD leg symptoms as pain, aching, heaviness or cramping during walking or exertion that improves with rest; calf claudication is a classic presentation.

source_row.stem: A client develops reproducible calf discomfort while walking that resolves after several minutes of rest. What does this pattern most strongly suggest?
